stories.title: Opinion: England and other nations are on the path toward eliminating hepatitis C. Why not the U.S.?
stories.summary: Eliminating hepatitis C is achievable ,  if the U.S. seriously invests in it, experts write.

stories.title: Opinion: How CMS plans to fix a major flaw in the 340B drug discount program
stories.summary: “A small, well-intended discount for safety net hospitals became a large institutional subsidy with expensive unintended consequences,” writes an HHS leader.

stories.title: Prevalence of Frequent Mental Distress and Physical Inactivity Among Adults Aged 18-29 Years - United States, 2012-2024
stories.summary: Poor mental health accounts for an estimated $300 billion in medical, pharmaceutical, and workplace- and suicide-related costs in the United States each year; promoting physical activity is an evidence-based approach to improving mental health.

stories.title: Roche goes beyond licensing in deal with Chinese biotech
stories.summary: Roche is partnering with Chinese startup Defand Therapeutics to discover new medicines.

stories.title: Seven principles for a critical transdisciplinary approach to planetary health
stories.summary: The ecological, social, and health crises of the Anthropocene demand approaches to knowledge that confront complexity, uncertainty, and structural injustice. Transdisciplinarity is an approach that can transcend disciplinary silos by integrating academic and non-academic knowledge.

stories.title: Sex-specific hemostatic responses and alterations of Platelet Distribution Width (PDW) and D-dimer in mild COVID-19, Malaria, and co-infection in a tropical setting: A case-control study in Port Harcourt, Nigeria
stories.summary: In malaria-endemic tropical regions, overlapping coagulopathy in COVID-19 and malaria poses management challenges with potential sex differences.

stories.title: Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it.
stories.summary: NPR's Michel Martin hosted a panel conversation about mental health and suicide in the Black community, exploring a difficult subject in deeply personal conversations.

stories.title: US Finally Signs Health Deal with Zambia, But Still Pursues Minerals Agreement
stories.summary: Zambia and the United States finally signed a bilateral health aid agreement on Thursday – after a 10-month delay as the US pushed for better access to the country’s minerals and changes to mining and agricultural regulations in exchange for health aid.

stories.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
stories.summary: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.

stories.title: ‘No plague case’ in Siberia, Russia tells WHO as assessments continue
stories.summary: Health authorities in Russia say there is “no plague case” in Siberia following reports last week that a lab technician had died of pneumonia of an unknown origin in the region, World Health Organization (WHO) officials said on Wednesday.

stories.title: 5 things civil rights data says about public schools
stories.summary: The federal Civil Rights Data Collection, for the first time in decades, tells us about the teacher workforce and reminds us racial disparities are still stark in American public schools.

stories.title: Assessing diagnostic accuracy of onchocerciasis rapid diagnostic tests using Bayesian latent class models
stories.summary: Onchocerciasis elimination programs increasingly rely on rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) that detect antibodies to the Ov16 antigen, yet the performance of currently available rapid tests remains uncertain.

stories.title: Coronary artery lesions in pediatrichus scrub typhus: A case series from Guangzhou, China
stories.summary: Scrub typhus, caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, is a mite-borne rickettsial infection endemic to the Asia-Pacific region. While its systemic complications are well documented, coronary artery lesions (CALs) associated with scrub typhus in children remain poorly characterized.

stories.title: Critical funding gap threatens health response in Yemen
stories.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) warned that significantly more resources are required to scale up its response in Yemen amid escalating conflict and rising needs.

stories.title: Deep learning applications in parasite microscopy: A scoping review
stories.summary: Parasitic diseases remain a significant contributor to the global burden of disease and conventional microscopy remains the gold standard for parasite detection. However, it is labour-intensive and dependent on skilled personnel, leading to variability in diagnostic accuracy.

stories.title: Detection of Acute Hepatitis C Outbreaks in California Using SaTScan: Statewide Spatiotemporal Analysis
stories.summary: Acute hepatitis C virus outbreaks in California are identified by local health jurisdictions through the investigation of cases reported by laboratories and health care providers to the state's public health surveillance system.

stories.title: DIY fertilizer is a blessing as farmers face steep prices due to the Iran war
stories.summary: It's hard enough being a small-scale farmer. Then the Iran war drove up fertilizer prices. So farmers are using a traditional Asian recipe to make their own. They call it a "labor of love."

stories.title: ER visits from people born outside the U.S. dropped after ICE raids
stories.summary: A new study found that visits by people born outside of the U.S. to three LA emergency rooms dropped precipitously after ICE raids increased last year.

stories.title: Expression of concern-Effect of Brazil's national human papillomavirus vaccination programme on the incidence of cervical cancer and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 in women aged 20-24 years: a population-based study
stories.summary: The Editors Of The Lancet Global Health.

stories.title: From El Niño-Southern Oscillation warning to proportionate health action
stories.summary: Rakesh A, Sreedharan R, Shumake-Guillemot J, Chungong S, Murray V, Ebi K.

stories.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
stories.summary: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

stories.title: Hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among high-risk patients in India, 2023-25: a multicentre prospective study
stories.summary: Melioidosis is not a nationally notifiable disease in India, and the absence of systematic surveillance has contributed to substantial under-recognition and fragmented epidemiological data.

stories.title: How to define a measles death
stories.summary: Historically, the CDC relied on state health departments' determination of measles deaths. Now, it's working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to create a clear definition.

stories.title: Kenya races to trace all contacts after first Ebola death, WHO official says
stories.summary: Kenya’s first Ebola death has triggered a race to trace everyone the victim came into contact with, as the United Nations and partners provide full support, the World Health Organization’s (WHO) top official in the country has told UN News in her first interview on the case.

stories.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
stories.summary: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.

stories.title: The WHO seeks more details on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia
stories.summary: The World Health Organization says it wants more information on what caused the death of an employee at a Russian plague research lab. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

stories.title: What is the pneumonic plague?
stories.summary: The ancient disease of plague is back in the headlines after the death this month of a Russian lab worker.

stories.title: WHO Asks Russia for More Information About Death of Plague Unit Employee
stories.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has asked the Russian government for more information about the death of an employee at a Siberian plague research unit, including details about the laboratory tests conducted on her, the WHO Director-General told a media briefing on Thursday.

stories.title: ‘Ebola takes the people children depend on’: UNICEF
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is robbing children of their loved ones – with some succumbing to the deadly disease themselves, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) reported on Tuesday.

stories.title: BREAKING: China Has Nominated Candidate for WHO Director General Whose Name Remains Undisclosed
stories.summary: China has nominated a prominent Chinese health official for WHO Director General in the 2027 elections, multiple diplomatic sources have confirmed to Health Policy Watch. But there are mixed reports about who that candidate actually may be.

stories.title: Extreme Heat Is Making Pregnancy More Dangerous for Mothers and Newborns
stories.summary: Nearly three in four maternal healthcare workers say extreme heat-related complications among pregnant women have increased over the past five years, according to a five-country survey released as climate ministers gathered in Fiji for the last major meeting before COP31.

stories.title: One million UK people who have never smoked are now vaping
stories.summary: Latest statistics also show, for the second year in a row, more over-16s vape than smoke.

stories.title: Opinion: I’m a doctor. Here’s what I want the public to know about AI tools and health care costs
stories.summary: “We can document honestly and still wind up inflating hospital bills,” writes a frustrated doctor.

stories.title: Opinion: Infectious disease expert: The mysterious pneumonia in Russia deserves attention, not panic
stories.summary: Chill out about reports about plague in Siberia, writes infectious disease doctor Krutika Kuppalli.
